pr_title: Restore Razor v3 whitespace behavior when langversion < 5. Fixes #28085
pr_body:
Fixes https://github.com/dotnet/aspnetcore/issues/28085

#### Description

The 5.0 SDK's Razor compiler is meant to be fully back-compatible with the 3.x SDK's Razor compiler. That is, for projects targeting `netcoreapp3.1`, the 5.0 Razor compiler output is meant to be functionally identical to what you'd get with the 3.1 Razor compiler, even though we have of course changed the Razor compiler in various ways for 5.0.

However, by mistake, one of the whitespace-stripping optimizations added for 5.0 is being applied to 3.x projects. This is a breaking change, albeit one that would rarely cause problems. In 5.0 there's a switch to control its behavior, but that switch doesn't exist in 3.x, so people targeting `netcoreapp3.1` are getting the new default optimization behavior without any way to turn it off.

#### Customer Impact

Reported by a customer at #28085. The effect was that, by removing some whitespace, we were breaking some HTML layout that explicitly depended on this whitespace.

The customer is working around it by pinning to the 3.1 SDK (e.g., via `global.json`). The other possible workaround would be changing the application code to avoid relying on this whitespace. Neither of these is the desired developer experience.

#### Regression?

Yes

#### Risk

Virtually none really. The new logic is just `if (version < 5) { old behavior } else { new behavior }` in a single place.

I guess it's theoretically possible that someone is already using the 5.0 SDK with a `netcoreapp3.1` target and has started relying on the new optimization, so by taking it away in a patch we'd be breaking them. However we can't have it both ways, and it's far more likely that people targeting `netcoreapp3.1` want the 3.x behavior. If they want the 5.0 behavior then they should upgrade the project to target `net5.0`.

## Review tip

The important change is in `ComponentWhitespacePass.cs`, and it's easiest to interpret if you suppress whitespace impacting the diff, i.e., use https://github.com/dotnet/aspnetcore/pull/28191/files?w=1#diff-9ede80967bfa15b1a1b9282ec00533be4bc3fa56fe255333c7412f1abd72edcb

issue_context.title: Blazor insignificant whitespace trimming is done by the 5.0 SDK even when not targeting 5.0
comments: It is not the 5.0 SDK alone. I installed 5.0 SDK 2 days ago, worked yesterday all day without any visibile changes and at the end of yesterday I upgraded VS from 16.7 to 16.8 - and now this morning "everything" looked different (some parts of my app got really ugly due to missing spaces).
and `@preservewhitespace true` at the top of my blazor file is not understood (using 3.1.9 since weeks).

@poke

> I know the ship has probably already sailed but maybe there’s a way to tell the SDK to keep the old tooling when targeting 3.1.

If you create a `global.json` file at the root of your project, you can tell `dotnet` to keep using the 3.1 SDK even though 5.0 is also installed.

That's just a short-term workaround. For 5.0.2 we should be able to include a proper fix for this so that 3.1-targeting apps get the 3.1 behavior even when using the 5.x SDK.

@SteveSandersonMS Yup, pinning the SDK works fine as a workaround (that’s how I verified this behavior in the first place).

The fix for 5.0.2 looks really promising! I expected this to be a lot more complicated to get both versions working. Thanks! :relaxed:

@springy76 There's something wrong with your installation of the .NET Core SDK. You may need to reinstall whatever specific SDK version you want to use. This isn't a Blazor-specific issue but rather is about the SDK itself, so if you have further trouble with that I'd recommend filing an issue at https://github.com/dotnet/sdk/issues. For reference, please see https://github.com/dotnet/sdk/issues/6180.

review_comments:
This fixes some tests that otherwise fail because the baselines would need to change. I don't see any clear reason for this particular set of unit tests to be hardcoded to razor language version 3, and it was only passing before because these tests happened not to exercise any behaviors that have changed between versions 3 and 5.

I could have fixed the broken tests by changing the baselines instead, but I think we actually want the test coverage to be for razor language version 5 as much as possible, except for the small number of tests that are explicitly about covering legacy behaviors.

This line is an example of something that is stripped out in the 5.0 behavior but not in the 3.1 behavior.

There are many such other examples throughout the baselines. If you want to see the exact diff on the baselines representing the changes between 3.1 and 5.0 behaviors, it's the baseline changes in this commit: https://github.com/dotnet/aspnetcore/pull/28191/commits/f90208d7774cc1ac9c8413b43fcf4e88bdee0a1e
